title: Basics before optimisations
statement: No optimisation, whether spacing, interleaving, multimedia or game elements, makes up for missing basics: unambiguous instruction, retrieval practice and mastery gating.
detail: The delivery platform ranks learning mechanisms in tiers: faultless communication, retrieval practice and mastery gating at 90% accuracy or more come first; spacing, interleaving, worked examples and feedback amplify them once that foundation is solid; novelty, multimedia and gamification help only under specific conditions (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0032-principles.qmd`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0027-learning-science.qmd`). It calls the first tier binary: no amount of the other tiers can compensate for a broken foundation, and features are liabilities where mechanisms are assets.
against: The ranking is the platform's own doctrine; nothing in these sources measures it.

evidence.quote: **Tip:** Tier 0 is binary. You either have faultless communication, retrieval practice, and mastery gating, or you do not. No amount of Tier 1 or 2 optimizations can compensate for a broken foundation. Features are liabilities; mechanisms are assets.
Students do not progress without demonstrating ≥90% accuracy on rigorous assessments.
The Education Endowment Foundation's April 2020 rapid review drew on 60 systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

It found teaching quality, clear explanations, scaffolding and feedback more consequential than the delivery clock; no clear difference between synchronous and asynchronous teaching emerged in the reviewed evidence.
The EEF says the underlying research did not measure learning during a global pandemic and was often drawn from contexts unlike 2020 closures.
